title: Capacity cadence experiments and autoscale ops playbook
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Summary: Create a repeatable quarterly cadence and a lightweight ops playbook for running controlled autoscale experiments against Dedicated pools. The goal is to reduce cost variance while preserving SLOs by testing conservative hedging policies, warm-pool strategies, and fast-fail fallbacks in a staged, measurable way.

Context: We have multiple overlaps in existing capacity docs (prewarm, reservoir, hedging) but no compact experiment cadence or a clear ops playbook that product + eng + SRE can run in a single quarter with measurable guardrails. Recent spikes during Q4 showed 16% deviation from forecast for certain pools and two production incidents where automated fallback didn't trigger cleanly. This ticket scopes a product-facing quarterly plan and the associated artifacts for run execution.

Scope:
- Define a 6-week experiment cadence template (plan, dry-run, canary, ramp, evaluate).
- Author an ops playbook with step-by-step runbook items for canary-to-burst transitions, rollback criteria, and post-mortem checklist.
- Design 3 experiment variants to test (conservative warm-pool hedging, predictive prewarm via short-term forecast, and burst-only fastpath with model fallbacks).
- Create dashboards and alerting templates for absolute and relative SLO regressions (latency P95, error rate, cost per token).
- Pilot the cadence in one dedicated pool (region-us-west2-ml1) with a single workload (autocomplete API) and capture results.

Out of scope: full fleet rollout, billing changes, or deep ML model tuning. This is focused on operating posture and cadence for autoscale experiments.

Stakeholders: PM (Leah Kim), Eng lead (Omar Khan), SRE (Maya Alvarez), Runtime (Kyle Benson), Console/Observability (Anita Rao), Support rotation representative (Jordan Price).

Artifacts and links:
- Draft playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/capacity-cadence-draft (placeholder)
- Pilot dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/DRW123/capacity-experiments (placeholder)
- Example PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8742 (pilot autoscale guardrails)
- Incident learnings: https://wiki.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-11-capacity-spike (placeholder)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Playbook doc exists and is approved by SRE and Runtime leads.
2) Cadence template (6-week) with roles, checkpoints, and rollback criteria published.
3) Pilot run executed against one dedicated pool and a runbook evidence log captured (links to dashboards and PRs).
4) Measurable metrics captured: baseline and experiment delta for latency P95, error rate, and cost per token.
5) Decision record with go/no-go guidance for broader rollout.
milestones:
M1: Draft playbook and cadence template (week 1-2)
M2: Implement dashboards and alerting templates (week 2-3)
M3: Dry-run operations with SRE (week 3-4)
M4: Canary pilot (week 4-5)
M5: Evaluate and produce decision record (week 6)
risks:
- Pilot could trigger regressions causing customer impact if rollback triggers fail.
- Observability gaps may make it hard to attribute cost delta to the experiment.
- Scheduling conflicts across SRE and runtime teams may delay the cadence.
- Incomplete KMS/audit configuration in private deployments could require gating for the on-prem variant.
